system.name: Revizor
system.one_liner: a prior model-based relational testing tool that detects speculative leaks by comparing contract and hardware traces of paired test-case inputs

components.name: RNG
components.role: random number generator seeding test-case generation

components.name: Test Case
components.role: generated test case containing a Program and an Input

components.name: Program
components.role: generated program part of the test case

components.name: Input
components.role: generated input part of the test case

components.name: Unicorn (Emulator)
components.role: the leakage model; emulates the test case to build the contract trace

components.name: Contract Trace
components.role: trace of observations permitted under the leakage contract

components.name: Target Defense (Simulator)
components.role: the executor; runs the test case on a simulator implementing the countermeasure under test

components.name: Hardware Trace
components.role: trace of actual hardware/microarchitectural observations produced by the executor

components.name: AND
components.role: combines the contract-trace equality check and the hardware-trace inequality check

components.name: Violation Found!
components.role: flagged result when contract traces match but hardware traces differ

flows.what: contract trace generated by the leakage model
hardware trace generated by the executor

content.key_idea: Revizor generates random test-case pairs, produces a contract trace and a hardware trace for each, and flags a violation when the contract traces are equal but the hardware traces differ, revealing a speculative leak.
content.reading_order: Left panel: a Generator builds a test case (Program+Input) from RNG; below it, the Leakage Model and Executor produce a Contract Trace and Hardware Trace respectively; the right panel shows the CTrace/HTrace comparison converging on Violation Found!.

palette.used_for: contract-trace side elements (Unicorn emulator, Contract Trace, CTrace A/B)
hardware-trace side elements (Target Defense, Hardware Trace, HTrace B)
the != inequality marker and the Violation Found! result ellipse

encoding.color_means: gold = contract-trace path, gray = hardware-trace path, red = mismatch/violation, purple/blue/orange = generator sub-components
encoding.emphasis: the red != marker and red Violation Found! ellipse highlight the detected leak
reusable_patterns: generator/model/executor pipeline feeding a paired-trace comparison for leak detection
weaknesses: no explicit arrows link the left pipeline boxes to the right-hand CTrace/HTrace comparison

evidence: consists of three main modules: (1) the test generator, which generates random programs and inputs
(2) the leakage model, which generates the contract traces
(3) the executor, which generates s from a simulator implementing the countermeasure

summary: This figure is an overview of Revizor, a prior model-based relational testing tool that AMuLeT builds on and re-describes in its background section. The text explains that Revizor consists of three main modules: a test generator that produces random programs and inputs, a leakage model that produces contract traces, and an executor that runs the test case on a simulator to produce hardware traces. In the figure, a Generator builds a Test Case (Program, Input) from an RNG; the Leakage Model panel shows Unicorn (Emulator) producing a Contract Trace, and the Executor panel shows a Target Defense (Simulator) producing a Hardware Trace. On the right, paired CTrace A/B are checked for equality while paired HTrace A/B are checked for inequality; an AND of both conditions flags Violation Found! when contract traces agree but hardware traces disagree, the relational-testing check AMuLeT extends to microarchitectural simulators.
summary_zh: 该图展示背景系统 Revizor 的三大模块：测试生成器、泄漏模型（生成 Contract Trace）与执行器（生成 Hardware Trace）；右侧比较成对输入的 CTrace 是否相等、HTrace 是否不等，二者同时成立即判定发现泄漏。
notes: This figure depicts Revizor, a prior-work system that AMuLeT's background section describes and builds on, not AMuLeT itself.
